concepts.name: Meaning of Budget
concepts.description: A budget is the annual financial statement of the government that estimates its expected receipts and expenditures for a financial year. It serves as a blueprint for managing public finances and implementing economic policies.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define a government budget and explain its purpose.

concepts.name: Objectives of Budget
concepts.description: The government prepares a budget to promote economic growth, maintain price stability, reduce unemployment, ensure equitable distribution of income, and provide public welfare.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the major objectives of a government budget.

concepts.name: Importance of Budget
concepts.description: A budget helps the government allocate resources efficiently, monitor public expenditure, and achieve developmental and social objectives.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to describe the importance of the budget in economic planning.

concepts.name: Budget Receipts
concepts.description: Budget receipts include all sources of government income such as tax revenue, non-tax revenue, borrowings, and recoveries of loans.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify government receipts into revenue and capital receipts.

concepts.name: Budget Expenditure
concepts.description: Government expenditure includes spending on administration, defense, infrastructure, education, healthcare, welfare schemes, and development projects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to classify government expenditure into revenue and capital expenditure.

concepts.name: Revenue and Capital Accounts
concepts.description: The budget separates receipts and expenditures into revenue and capital accounts to clearly present the government's financial position.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to differentiate between revenue account and capital account.

concepts.name: Balanced Budget
concepts.description: A balanced budget occurs when the government's total receipts are equal to its total expenditures during a financial year.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the concept of a balanced budget.

concepts.name: Deficit Budget
concepts.description: A deficit budget arises when government expenditure exceeds government receipts, requiring borrowing or other financing methods.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the causes and implications of a deficit budget.

concepts.name: Surplus Budget
concepts.description: A surplus budget occurs when government receipts exceed expenditures, leaving excess funds after meeting all planned expenses.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to distinguish between surplus and deficit budgets.

concepts.name: Fiscal Deficit
concepts.description: Fiscal deficit is the excess of the government's total expenditure over its total receipts excluding borrowings. It indicates the amount the government needs to borrow to finance its spending.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to define fiscal deficit and explain its significance.

concepts.name: Public Debt
concepts.description: Public debt consists of money borrowed by the government from internal and external sources to finance budget deficits and development projects.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the relationship between fiscal deficit and public debt.

concepts.name: Fiscal Responsibility
concepts.description: Prudent fiscal management helps maintain economic stability by controlling deficits, reducing unnecessary expenditure, and ensuring sustainable public finances.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the importance of fiscal responsibility in government finance.

topics.title: Role of Budget in Economic Development

concepts.name: Resource Allocation
concepts.description: The government budget directs financial resources toward priority sectors such as education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure, and social welfare.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how the budget supports efficient resource allocation.

concepts.name: Income Redistribution
concepts.description: Through taxation and welfare expenditure, the government budget aims to reduce income inequality and promote social justice.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain how the budget contributes to equitable income distribution.

concepts.name: Economic Stabilization
concepts.description: Government budgets help control inflation, stimulate employment, promote investment, and maintain overall macroeconomic stability.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the role of the budget in maintaining economic stability.

concepts.name: Understanding Government Budget
concepts.description: This chapter introduces the meaning, objectives, components, receipts, expenditures, budget balances, fiscal deficit, and the role of the budget in promoting economic development and public welfare.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to analyze the structure of a government budget and evaluate its role in economic planning, fiscal management, and national development.
